Midjourney has been the go-to AI image generator for designers and architects since it launched, mainly because it was the only option worth considering for a while. Even nowadays, it’s widely known as somewhat of a gold standard.

But is it still?

Also, now that the free tier is long gone, an even bigger question is whether Midjourney pricing actually makes sense for your workflow. Does what you're paying line up with what you're getting?

We build [AI tools for visualization](https://www.myarchitectai.com/), so we have a clear insight into what AI can and can't do, as well as what it should and shouldn't cost. So we broke down every Midjourney plan to reveal where the value holds up, and flagged the details that tend to catch people off guard.

Once you decide on the subscription tier, read our guide on [prompting Midjourney](https://www.myarchitectai.com/blog/midjourney-architecture-prompts).

## **How much does Midjourney cost in 2026?**

As with most tools today, Midjourney pricing is structured around subscription tiers, so you find four monthly options. The core mechanic it’s based on is GPU time; essentially you're paying for priority access to the servers that run the model. Your plan equals the number of hours of that access you get per month.

That's a different model from tools that charge per image or per credit. In practice, it means a standard image generation in fast mode costs roughly 1 minute of GPU time. Higher-resolution outputs and upscaling operations consume more.

  

| Plan | Monthly | Annual (per mo.) | Fast GPU hours | Relax mode | Stealth mode | Concurrent jobs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $10 | $8  | 3.3 hrs (~200 images) | No  | No  | 3   |
| Standard | $30 | $24 | 15 hrs (~900 images) | Unlimited | No  | 3   |
| Pro | $60 | $48 | 30 hrs (~1,800 images) | Unlimited | Yes | 12  |
| Mega | $120 | $96 | 60 hrs (~3,600 images) | Unlimited | Yes | 12  |

Annual billing knocks 20% off all plans; hence, if you know you'll use Midjourney consistently, paying yearly on the Standard or Pro plan is straightforward math. In any other case, extra fast GPU time is also available on any tier at $4 per hour. It covers you if you run out mid-month, but we’ll get back to the real cost of that part.

## **Fast GPU time vs Relax mode**

This distinction is more important than the headline differences in Midjourney pricing tiers. It's the first thing that separates those tiers in practice.

### **Fast mode**

It generates images in 10 to 30 seconds and draws directly from your monthly GPU hour allocation. In practice, each standard image costs roughly a minute of fast time. Upscaling and running variations can each take 2 to 4 minutes; the same applies to generating at higher resolutions. But once your fast hours are gone, they're gone, no rollover to the next billing cycle.

### **Relax mode**

This mode uses shared GPU resources during off-peak periods. Generation takes anywhere from 0 to 30 minutes ([per Midjourney's own docs](https://docs.midjourney.com/hc/en-us/articles/32016412137741-GPU-Speed-Fast-Relax-Turbo)) which in practice typically translates to 1 to 10 minutes depending on server load. It doesn't consume your fast hour budget at all, and on Standard, Pro, and Mega plans, it's unlimited.

While not exactly stealth, the Relax mode handles ideation and iteration for most workflows just fine. Midjourney pricing tiers unlock this mode on the Standard plan at $30/month, and it notably changes the value of the subscription compared to Basic. Now, speaking of that:

## **Which of the Midjourney pricing plans actually fits your work?**

### **Basic ($10/month)**

Three and a half hours of fast GPU time counts for roughly 200 images. When those hours run out, generation stops until the next billing cycle (unless you purchase additional fast hours at $4 each). There is no Relax mode to switch to and continue generating at a slower pace.

Basic works as an entry point to test the platform and evaluate whether the image quality justifies committing to a higher tier. For any sustained creative or professional use, it runs out fast, so it’s possible that you’ll move off it even within the first month.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/656ce9577513edfecc6bb74a/6a8706268832dfbbb3c40c60_midjourney.avif)

### **Standard ($30/month)**

This is where Midjourney pricing starts to make practical sense. Fifteen fast hours give you roughly 900 images in that mode. Relax mode meanwhile covers anything that doesn't need to come out in an instant. For solo creators, including architects who generate concept visuals, the Standard plan handles consistent output reasonably well.

What the Standard plan doesn’t cover is the Stealth Mode, and before you think “The fast is fast enough,” this is **_not_** about speed. Every image you generate on Standard is publicly visible in Midjourney's gallery. For personal work or experimental projects, that's mostly fine. But for client-facing design work and in general situations where confidentiality matters, it's not.

### **Pro ($60/month)**

The jump from $30 to $60 is steep, but it comes with two things that matter for professional use. The first is Stealth Mode, which keeps your generated images off the public gallery. The second is 12 concurrent jobs, up from 3, which makes a lot of difference when you're running batch generations or iterating on multiple concepts in parallel.

For design professionals doing client work, Pro is effectively the minimum viable tier. That reality makes the $60 price point the _actual starting cost_ for this case, regardless of the listed Midjourney prices.

## Article Content

Alright, let's get down to brass tacks. If you're serious about using Midjourney, you need to understand its pricing. It’s a subscription-only club now, with monthly plans kicking off at **$10 for the Basic plan** and scaling up to **$120 for the Mega plan**.

For those ready to commit, there's a **20% discount** if you pay annually. Every tier, except for the entry-level one, also gets you unlimited "Relax Mode" generations—a feature we’ll unpack a bit later.

### A Snapshot of Midjourney AI Pricing Plans

![A tablet displays a pricing page with Basic, Standard, Pro, and Mega plans, each offering a 20% annual discount.](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Flfbxotgojyqeeyxwmcod.supabase.co%2Fstorage%2Fv1%2Fobject%2Fpublic%2Fblog-images%2Fmidjourney-ai-pricing%2Ff8cf7e99550c.jpg&w=1080&q=75)

For any performance marketer or creative team, figuring out what Midjourney costs is the first step to integrating AI visuals into your workflow. The days of the free trial are long gone. Instead, Midjourney has opted for a paid structure that guarantees predictable access and, frankly, a much better experience by ensuring the servers aren't overwhelmed.

This move has paid off, big time. By shifting to a four-tier subscription model, Midjourney’s annual revenue reportedly shot up from $50 million in 2022 to an estimated **$500 million in 2025**—that’s a staggering **66.7% year-over-year jump**. This surge is backed by a community of over 21 million registered users. You can dig into more of this explosive growth data over at checkthat.ai.

### Breaking Down the Tiers

To help you figure out where you fit, here’s a quick comparison of the four subscription plans on offer.

### Midjourney Subscription Plans at a Glance (2026)

| Plan | Monthly Price | Annual Price (20% Off) | Fast GPU Time / Month | Relax Mode | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Basic** | $10 | $8 / mo | 3.3 hrs (~200 images) | No  | Individuals & hobbyists getting started |
| **Standard** | $30 | $24 / mo | 15 hrs (~900 images) | Unlimited | Freelancers & small teams needing flexibility |
| **Pro** | $60 | $48 / mo | 30 hrs (~1,800 images) | Unlimited | Agencies needing volume & privacy (Stealth) |
| **Mega** | $120 | $96 / mo | 60 hrs (~3,600 images) | Unlimited | Enterprise teams with high-throughput needs |

As you can see, each plan is built for a different kind of user, from someone just dipping their toes in the water to a full-blown agency cranking out visuals around the clock. Let's look a little closer at who each plan is really for.

*   **The Basic Plan:** This is your entry point. It's perfect for individuals and hobbyists who are just exploring what's possible. You get enough "Fast GPU" time for about **200 images** a month.
*   **The Standard Plan:** This is the crowd favorite and for good reason. It’s the sweet spot for most freelancers and small teams, offering a big jump in Fast GPU hours and, crucially, unlocking unlimited Relax Mode.
*   **The Pro Plan:** Built for professionals and agencies who can't have their work showing up in the public feed. This plan introduces "Stealth Mode," which keeps all your creations private, a must for client work.
*   **The Mega Plan:** The top-tier solution for large-scale operations. It’s all about maximum throughput, with the most Fast GPU hours and the highest number of concurrent jobs you can run.

For marketers, picking the right plan is key to scaling ad creative development. It’s a process that mirrors the kind of efficiency you see in the [best AI tools for digital marketing](https://www.adstellar.ai/blog/best-ai-tools-for-digital-marketing), allowing your team to go from brainstorming to bulk visual creation without hitting any walls.

## Decoding Midjourney Plans From Basic to Mega

Choosing a Midjourney plan isn’t just about picking a price. It’s about matching the right tool to the job. Each tier is built for a different kind of creative workflow, from someone just testing the waters to a full-blown agency pumping out visuals daily. Getting this choice right is the key to unlocking Midjourney's potential without burning through your budget.

Think of the **Fast GPU hours** in each plan as the fuel in your creative engine. Every image you generate uses a tiny bit of this high-octane fuel, letting you create at top speed. The more fuel in your tank, the faster you can go.

### The Basic Plan: Your Starter Kit

At **$10 per month**, the **Basic plan** is the perfect on-ramp for anyone curious about AI art. It's really for individuals, hobbyists, or marketers just starting to see how AI-generated images could fit into their workflow.

You get **3.3 hours of Fast GPU time**, which translates to roughly **200 images per month**. This is plenty for:

*   **Getting your feet wet:** Learning how to write effective prompts and figuring out Midjourney’s distinct style.
*   **Personal projects:** Creating a few unique graphics for a social media profile, a personal blog, or just for fun.
*   **One-off needs:** Grabbing a handful of images for a presentation or a small internal project.

But here’s the catch: there's no "Relax Mode." Once your Fast GPU hours are used up, you’re done generating until your plan renews. This makes the Basic plan a tough sell for anyone with consistent deadlines or ongoing creative needs.
